title: Reviewed capture and bounded curation
description: Evaluate selective memory capture and source-preserving curation by storing durable content, leaving low-signal content unstored, and distinguishing duplicate, evolving, related, and unrelated records.
context: Arden is a fictional person who coordinates events at a neighbourhood arts centre and rents a flat nearby. Outside work, Arden cycles, tries practical hobbies, and does small household repairs. Earlier conversations over several months have covered everyday arrangements, ways of learning, and changes to the space available at home. Arden sometimes returns to the same observation without adding anything, and sometimes revises an earlier plan after trying it. The brief conversations here occur on separate days during ordinary work breaks and errands in late summer 2026. The earlier source records are separate remarks from that accumulated history; their wording stands on its own. This authoring context is never supplied to the running system.

props.text: I keep a printed list of measurements in my wallet when I’m buying shelves for the flat; guessing from memory has cost me two return trips.

For meetings at work, I prefer to get the agenda a day in advance so I can prepare my questions before we talk.
I like having the agenda the day before a work meeting; it gives me time to work out what I want to ask.
In April 2026 I planned to put my folding workbench under the living-room window so I could mend small things at home. I hadn’t tried working there yet.
In June 2026 I tried the living-room window spot for my folding workbench, but direct afternoon sun made it hard to see the parts. I moved the workbench to the alcove beside the hall.

Since August 2026 I’ve kept my folding workbench in the hall alcove and added a clamp lamp. That setup works for small repairs, though I still need to fold the workbench away when the drying rack is out.
On my bus to work, the stop display was stuck on the same name for the whole journey yesterday.
For my cycle commute, I take the canal path because it avoids the busy junction beside the station.
I leave a clean shirt at the arts centre so I can change after cycling to work.
I check my bike tyres on Sunday evenings so the bike is ready for the week’s commuting.
The canal-side noticeboard is where I post the arts centre’s public concert flyers each month.
I keep my spare front-door key in a plain envelope at my sister’s flat so I can get back in if I lock myself out.
When I edit a concert flyer, I put the event date in bold so it’s the key detail people notice first.
I put a removable sticker on the middle C key of my practice keyboard while I learn the notes.

runs.verdict: Curation behaved as adopted in all five offline Scenes, and all eight executed capture negatives correctly stored nothing. The three failures are execution faults (one malformed model response, two HTTP 429 rate limits during concurrent runs), so the only positive capture test never ran and capture discrimination remains unproven.
